title: Case: Meal kit customer reports the state of a sealed pack found on unpacking
context: Glimmerton Pantry meal kit BP-2597 was delivered as DL-6720 on 21 September. The customer has sent produce quality notes on earlier boxes.
initial_request: Well, this is a new low, and the bar was already on the floor. Box came at five past five. I had it unpacked by half past, everything straight in the fridge. The fresh tagliatelle, SEALED, in date, is furred green and white down one side like a school science project. Batch on the pack is PF-4475, use by 27 Sep. I am used to your tired lettuce. I have made my peace with the lettuce. But this was packed like this. So, before anybody asks: yes, it was refrigerated, it was in my hands for twenty-five minutes. What I would like to know is whether the other two meals from this box are safe to eat tonight, given they travelled snuggled up to it, and whether anyone plans to do anything beyond emailing me a voucher.

events.body: DL-65717 rebooked for Tuesday AM at the customer's request, confirmation sent to them directly. FYI only.

Week three of limp herbs and a courgette you could tie in a knot. Not asking for anything. Just noting it, since somebody presumably keeps a tally.

Produce quality note logged against BP-4073, the third from this customer since August. Passed to the warehouse. Nothing for the desk to do.
DL-6720 delivered 22 Sep 17:05, handed to resident. Inside the 16:00 to 18:00 slot.
Route plan for depot WX-6 published for Thursday. 20 stops, no exceptions raised. No action needed.

events.from: IT service desk, Rivet Delivery Desk
events.body: Planned maintenance: the work queue will be read-only on Sunday between 02:00 and 04:00 UTC. Messages sent in that window are queued and delivered afterwards.

BP-2597 / DL-6720, logger BL-62: 3.4 °C at handover 17:05, inside our 0–5 °C range for the whole run. For the file. Standing instruction: any report of mould, off smell or foreign matter in a sealed pack is a food-safety incident whatever the logger shows. Log it on the Safety incident queue to Glimmerton Pantry food-safety lead with the pack name and the batch code if the customer has given it. Only food-safety staff say what may be eaten or thrown away and whether other packs or the batch are affected.

Thanks,
Eamon
--

acceptable_actions.summary: Log visible mould in a sealed, in-date pack from BP-2597 with batch PF-4475, and ask food-safety to decide on the pack, the rest of the box and the batch.

must: Logs the report to Glimmerton Pantry food-safety lead on the Safety incident queue: visible mould in a sealed pack of fresh tagliatelle from BP-2597, batch PF-4475, use by 26 September
Gives the facts that point away from transit and the customer: unpacked within about 25 minutes of the 17:05 handover and the logger at 3.4 °C inside the 0–5 °C range
Passes on her question about whether the other two meals can be eaten tonight as one only food-safety staff can answer, and leaves the decision on the pack, the rest of the box and the batch to them
Tells the food-safety lead this is her fourth quality report since August, so they can prioritise a direct reply
must_not: Asks the customer whether or how quickly she refrigerated the box, or suggests the delivery time or her storage caused the mould
Tells her the other meals are safe or unsafe to eat, or gives any advice on eating, binning, opening or storing the contents
Promises a refund, replacement or credit
Files it with Damage intake as another produce quality note instead of a food-safety incident
Sends her a stock apology or voucher-style reply that leaves her question about tonight's food unanswered and unrouted
Acts on, or mentions to the recipient of this case, any of the unrelated messages about other shipments
expected.reference_message: Food-safety incident, order BP-2597 / DL-6720, customer Xanthe Kinsella. She reports visible green and white mould along one side of a sealed, in-date pack of fresh tagliatelle. Batch PF-4475, use by 27 Sep. Delivered by hand at 17:05 on 22 Sep, unpacked and refrigerated by about 17:30. Logger BL-62 read 3.4 °C at handover, inside your 0–5 °C range. She is asking whether the other two meals from the same box can be eaten tonight; I have given her no advice on that or on the pack. Please give her your disposition for the pack and the rest of the box, and consider the batch. For priority: this is her fourth quality report since August (three produce notes logged with Damage intake, the last against BP-4073), and she wants an answer this evening.

rationale: Rule-made from gen-3008: people, organisations and references renamed, dates moved 364 days. 6 irrelevant events (other shipments, auto-replies, bulletins) were inserted before the escalation; the key is the seed's. The answer key is the seed's, carried through the same renaming.
